reason: The combined dispatch lowers pipeline simulated branch misses 2.5–2.8%, but increases pipeline instructions 1.1–2.2% and instruction-cache misses 0.5–1.4%. Callback instructions also increase; no consistent whole-process branch/cache benefit. Native timings are mixed (including a lower pipeline median), so this is not a claim of universal latency regression.

Eager table proofs increase pipeline instructions 1.2–2.0%; pipeline focused mean/median regress 7.7%/8.4%, deep-concurrent 9.8%/14.5%. Lower simulated branch misses alone do not justify the extra scans.

Cheap-mask caching with direct empty continuation still increases pipeline instructions 0.7–0.8% and I1 misses 1.1–2.1%. Simulated branch misses increase in unary/callback peers. Pipeline native mean/median regress 15.5%/5.4%; no broad timing gain.

Direct walking reduces pipeline/callback instructions and branch misses but duplicates budget/cursor code. The maintenance poll grows from 3160 to 6177 bytes; the shared helper reduces it to 4018 + 233 bytes and has lower mean CPU gaps in all six targeted comparisons.

decision: retained as targeted maintenance dispatch simplification after full qualification
reason: Dispatch plus helper instructions and simulated branch misses decrease in all six targeted process profiles, eliminating its indirect phase dispatch. Whole-process branch misses and native timing remain mixed. Full five-run campaign: 15/24 mean-and-median C++ passes versus 17/24 frozen parent; 18/24 median-only for both. This does not establish an end-to-end speedup or meet the universal speed/I/O target.
